body.proof_tex:
The product weights in Definition \(\mathrm{fitted\mbox{-}center}\) satisfy the detailed-balance ratios (1).  Irreducibility makes their normalizations the unique invariant laws.  At \(p'=p\) and \(M=M_N\), they are therefore \(\rho_{0,N}\) and \(\rho_{1,N}\), which proves \(\vartheta_N(p;M_N)=\theta_N\).

Let \(\mu_{1,N}(p';M)=\sum_k(k/N)\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}(k)\).  For fixed \(M\), let \(v_N\) be the centered solution of
\[
 -\mathcal A_{1,N}^{p',M}v_N=k/N-\mu_{1,N}(p';M).
\]
Differentiating the finite identity \(\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}\mathcal A_{1,N}^{p',M}=0\), and applying the differentiated signed measure to \(v_N\), gives for each rate coordinate \(r\)
\[
 \partial_r\mu_{1,N}(p';M)
 =\mathbb E_{\rho_{1,N}^{p',M}}
   [\{\partial_r\mathcal A_{1,N}^{p',M}\}v_N].                  \tag{13}
\]
This is ordinary differentiation of a finite sum; no interchange of an infinite limit is involved.

At \(p'=p,M=M_N\), one has \(v_N(k)=u_{1,N}(s_{1,N}(k))/\sqrt N\).  If
\[
 R_N^+(k)=N\{v_N(k+1)-v_N(k)\},
 \qquad R_N^-(k)=N\{v_N(k)-v_N(k-1)\},
\]
then (13) becomes
\[
 \begin{split}
 \partial_\lambda\mu_{1,N}&=\mathbb E[(1-K_{1,N}/N)R_N^+(K_{1,N})],\\
 \partial_\tau\mu_{1,N}&=-\mathbb E[(K_{1,N}/N)R_N^-(K_{1,N})],\\
 \partial_\nu\mu_{1,N}&=-\mathbb E[(\min\{K_{1,N},M_N\}/N)R_N^-(K_{1,N})].
 \end{split}                                                     \tag{14}
\]
The edge-average limits of Lemma \(\mathrm{finite\mbox{-}chain\mbox{-}poisson\mbox{-}controls}\) imply, uniformly,
\[
 \nabla_p\mu_{1,N}(p;M_N)
 \longrightarrow ((1-a)H,-aH,-aH)^{\mathsf T}.                 \tag{15}
\]
The control product law is binomial with mean \(Na_0\), so its normalized mean has gradient
\[
 \nabla a_0=((1-a_0)/d,-a_0/d,0)^{\mathsf T}.                   \tag{16}
\]
Subtracting (15) from (16) proves the derivative limit (11), exactly in the displayed coordinates of \(A\).

It remains to justify the uniform Taylor remainder later used with this derivative.  For either product law, write \(S_r(k)=\partial_r\log w_N(k)\).  The one-step increments in \(k\) of \(S_r\) and of \(\partial_sS_r\) are bounded uniformly on \([c/2,2C]^3\): this follows term by term from
\[
 \partial_\lambda\log w_N(k)=k/\lambda,
 \quad
 \partial_\tau\log w_{1,N}(k)
 =-\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{j}{\tau j+\nu\min(j,M)},
 \quad
 \partial_\nu\log w_{1,N}(k)
 =-\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{\min(j,M)}{\tau j+\nu\min(j,M)}.           \tag{17}
\]
The control formulas are the corresponding special cases.  For arbitrary interior \(M\), the count-scale drift \(B_k-D_k\) decreases by at least \(\lambda'+\tau'\geq c\) at each step and all jump rates are at most \(6CN\) on the enlarged rate box.  Centering at the unique sign-change point of that drift and applying the generator successively to its second, fourth, and sixth powers gives \(\mathbb E|K-\mathbb EK|^r\leq C_rN^{r/2}\) for \(r\leq6\); the odd moments follow by Hölder's inequality.  This drift calculation does not require the capacity to lie in a critical window.  Consequently every centered \(S_r(K)\) and centered \(\partial_sS_r(K)\) has its \(r\)-th moment bounded by a constant times \(N^{r/2}\).

Finite-sum differentiation gives
\[
 \partial_r\mathbb E f(K)=\operatorname{Cov}(f(K),S_r(K))
\]
and
\[
 \partial_s\partial_r\mathbb E f(K)
 =\mathbb E[(f-\mathbb Ef)(S_r-\mathbb ES_r)(S_s-\mathbb ES_s)]
  +\operatorname{Cov}(f,\partial_sS_r).                          \tag{18}
\]
Taking \(f(K)=K/N\), Hölder's inequality, the sixth-moment bounds, and (17) bound the first term in (18) by \(C\sqrt N\) and the second by \(C\).  Applying this to both arms proves (12).
